title: Viewing the Post-Quantum Cryptography Visibility Report

blocks.text: To view the Post-Quantum Cryptography Visibility Report, from the navigation menu, go to Analytics > Reports > Interactive Reports > Standard Reports > Web Activity > Post-Quantum Cryptography Visibility.
You can hover over the chart’s data in the report and click on it to gain more insights. To view information either in the form of logs or charts:

blocks.item: Click View Logs to view the chart’s logs on the Insights Logs page. To go back to the report, click Back to Original.
Click Analyze Chart to view the chart on the Insights Logs page. To go back to the report, click Back to Original.

blocks.text: The Post-Quantum Cryptography Visibility Report allows you to view information from the following perspectives:

blocks.item: You can gain insights into the distribution of transactions showing the customer Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) readiness. The graphs show a comparison between the PQC algorithm and the Classical Key Exchange algorithm of your organization's web traffic.
Classical: When you click within the Classical section, you can view all transactions where the Client Key Exchange has either the Classical or Unknown type set.
PQC: When you click within the PQC section of the chart, you can view all transactions where the Client Key Exchange offer has either the PQC or the Hybrid type set.

You can gain insights into the client-side negotiated PQC or Hybrid Key Exchange algorithms that are ranked by their frequency in your transactions. This chart allows you to see which quantum-safe cryptographic methods are most prevalent in your network traffic.
3. Top Users with PQC Key Exchange

You can gain insights into user activity related to PQC or Hybrid Key Exchange algorithms. The data presented ranks users based on their total transaction count, offering a clear overview of who is most frequently engaging with these advanced cryptographic methods.

You can view insights into the TLS versions used for communications between the client and Public Service Edge for Internet & SaaS (ZIA). The charts help you analyze trends over time to identify any potential vulnerabilities or areas for improvement in security posture.
PQC support requires TLS 1.3 and cannot be negotiated in TLS 1.2 and earlier versions.

You can view insights into the TLS versions used for communications between the Public Service Edge and the server. The charts help you analyze trends over time to identify any potential vulnerabilities or areas for improvement in security posture.
PQC support requires TLS 1.3 and cannot be negotiated in TLS 1.2 and earlier versions.
